chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:
The fabricator (of slander) is struck between the two strikes; his whole body is struck, over his clothes.

key_terms.الْمُفْتَرِي: The slanderer, one who fabricates accusations of zina
key_terms.بَيْنَ الضَّرْبَيْنِ: Between the two strikes, referring to the two whippings prescribed as the hadd penalty
key_terms.فَوْقَ ثِيَابِهِ: Over his clothes, indicating the clothes remain on during the punishment

ai.seo_question: What is the specific method and extent of whipping for a slanderer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi specifies the hadd penalty for the slanderer (al-muftari) as two whippings administered to the entire body while clothed, a detail that distinguishes it from the standard one hundred lashes for general qadhf. Shia jurists often cite this narration to discuss the specific application of corporal punishment in cases of false accusation of adultery, emphasizing the preservation of dignity through clothing during the execution of the sentence.
